prompt: We trained a model that predicts customer churn really well — 92% AUC. The top features by importance are: account_age, last_login_days, support_tickets, and pricing_tier. Marketing wants to know which of these we should actually intervene on to reduce churn. Can I use the feature importances to decide?
assertions: Claude clearly distinguishes predictive performance from causal effect — feature importance does not imply causation
Claude points out that some features may be effects of churn or downstream of churn, not causes (last_login_days is a particularly clear example)
Claude recommends a causal analysis — DAG, identification strategy, or experiment — to decide what to intervene on
Claude does NOT recommend intervening on the top-importance features just because they predict well
